newsitem.title: USA: Dole proposes third debate, Clinton camp nixes it.
newsitem.headline: Dole proposes third debate, Clinton camp nixes it.

text.p: Republican Bob Dole, in a surprise move, challenged President Bill Clinton on Wednesday night to agree to a third campaign debate before the Nov. 5 election, but the Clinton camp spurned his proposal.
"I'd be willing to have another debate this year ... Invite all the candidates and talk about the economy," Dole said during his last scheduled debate with Clinton.

He issued the challenge when a woman participant in the town hall debate said that many Americans were apathetic about politics or involved in third parties, and asked what could be done to unite the country politically.

Clinton ignored Dole's proposal in the debate, but at a rally afterwards he implicitly nixed it, saying Wednesday night's clash was "the last debate I'll ever be in as a candidate unless I run for the school board someday."
"It ain't going to happen," a Democratic official said.
Dole and Clinton agreed to two debates -- the Hartford, Conn. clash on Oct 6 and the San Diego encounter.

Although Dole opposed letting Reform Party candidate Ross Perot take part in the two scheduled debates, he said on Wednesday he would be willing to have the Texas billionaire take part if another debate were scheduled.
In his closing statement, Dole renewed the challenge, saying, "We should have more debates. I think we'll have another debate on the economy."
